title: 1 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 18.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 18, after how many years did the word of the LORD come to Elijah?
questions.correctAnswer: Three years
questions.explanation: The word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year as stated in 1 Kings 18:1.

questions.question: What was Elijah instructed to do by the LORD in the third year?
questions.correctAnswer: Shew thyself unto Ahab
questions.explanation: The LORD told Elijah to go and shew himself unto Ahab in 1 Kings 18:1.

questions.question: What condition was the land in when Elijah showed himself to Ahab?
options: It was a time of peace
The land was full of grass
questions.correctAnswer: There was a sore famine
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:2 states there was a sore famine in Samaria at that time.

questions.question: Who was the governor of Ahab's house mentioned in 1 Kings 18?
questions.correctAnswer: Obadiah
questions.explanation: Obadiah is named as the governor of Ahab's house in 1 Kings 18:3.

questions.question: True or False: Obadiah feared the LORD greatly.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:3 explicitly states that Obadiah feared the LORD greatly.

questions.question: What did Obadiah do when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the LORD?
options: He hid one hundred prophets in a cave and fed them
He killed the prophets of Baal
questions.correctAnswer: He hid one hundred prophets in a cave and fed them
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:4 states Obadiah hid a hundred prophets by fifty in a cave and fed them with bread and water.

questions.question: What was Ahab's purpose in sending Obadiah to all fountains and brooks?
options: To find water for the people
To find grass to save the horses and mules alive
questions.correctAnswer: To find grass to save the horses and mules alive
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:5 explains Ahab sent Obadiah to find grass so they would not lose all their beasts.

questions.question: How did Ahab and Obadiah divide the land when searching for grass?
options: Ahab took the north, Obadiah took the south
Ahab went one way by himself, Obadiah went another way by himself
questions.correctAnswer: Ahab went one way by himself, Obadiah went another way by himself
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 18:6, they divided the land and went separate ways.

questions.question: Who did Obadiah meet on the way while searching for grass?
questions.correctAnswer: Elijah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:7 states Obadiah met Elijah on his way.

questions.question: True or False: Obadiah was afraid that Ahab would kill him if he told him Elijah was present.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:9 and 18:14, Obadiah expresses fear that Ahab would slay him if Elijah was not found.

questions.question: What did Elijah say to Obadiah to assure him about showing himself to Ahab?
options: I will surely shew myself unto him today
I will flee to another land
questions.correctAnswer: I will surely shew myself unto him today
questions.explanation: Elijah declared he would surely show himself to Ahab that day in 1 Kings 18:15.

questions.question: What did Obadiah do after his conversation with Elijah?
options: He went to meet Ahab and told him about Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: He went to meet Ahab and told him about Elijah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:16 states Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him Elijah was present.

questions.question: True or False: When Ahab saw Elijah, he accused him of troubling Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:17 records Ahab asking Elijah if he is the one troubling Israel.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 18, which of the following events happened first?
options: Obadiah hid the prophets in a cave
Elijah called for a contest on Mount Carmel
The fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Obadiah hid the prophets in a cave
questions.explanation: The hiding of prophets by Obadiah occurred early in the chapter as per 1 Kings 18:4, before the later events.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah feared Ahab and tried to avoid showing himself to him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elijah boldly declared he would show himself to Ahab that day (1 Kings 18:15), showing no fear.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What accusation did King Ahab make against Elijah when he saw him?
options: That Elijah was the one troubling Israel
That Elijah was hiding from him
That Elijah was a false prophet
That Elijah had fled the land
questions.correctAnswer: That Elijah was the one troubling Israel
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:17, Ahab directly asked Elijah, 'Art thou he that troubleth Israel?', accusing him of causing trouble in the nation.

questions.question: According to Elijah's response to Ahab, who truly caused trouble in Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahab and his father's house
questions.explanation: Elijah stated in 1 Kings 18:18 that he had not troubled Israel, but rather Ahab and his father's house had, because they forsook the LORD's commandments and followed Baalim.

questions.question: How many prophets of Baal did Elijah ask to be gathered to Mount Carmel?
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:19, Elijah instructed to gather four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal to Mount Carmel for the contest.

questions.question: What was Elijah's challenge to the people regarding their worship in 1 Kings 18:21?
options: To decide whether to follow the LORD or Baal
To choose which prophet to believe
questions.correctAnswer: To decide whether to follow the LORD or Baal
questions.explanation: Elijah asked the people in 1 Kings 18:21 how long they would hesitate between two opinions, urging them to follow the LORD if He is God or Baal if he is god.

questions.question: What did Elijah claim about himself in contrast to the prophets of Baal?
options: He was the only remaining prophet of the LORD
He was the most powerful prophet
He was a prophet of Baal
questions.correctAnswer: He was the only remaining prophet of the LORD
questions.explanation: Elijah declared in 1 Kings 18:22 that he alone remained a prophet of the LORD, while Baal had four hundred and fifty prophets.

questions.question: What was the condition Elijah set for the bullocks used in the contest?
options: They were to be cut in pieces and laid on wood without fire
They were to be cooked over a fire before the call
They were to be left whole and untouched
They were to be sacrificed by Baal's prophets first
questions.correctAnswer: They were to be cut in pieces and laid on wood without fire
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:23, Elijah instructed that the bullocks were to be cut in pieces and laid on wood with no fire underneath, so the true God would reveal Himself by fire.

questions.question: What was the purpose of calling on the name of their gods during the contest according to Elijah?
options: To see which god would answer by fire
To test the strength of the people
questions.correctAnswer: To see which god would answer by fire
questions.explanation: Elijah declared in 1 Kings 18:24 that the God who answered by fire would be recognized as the true God.

questions.question: How long did the prophets of Baal call on their god without any answer?
questions.correctAnswer: From morning until noon
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 18:26, the prophets of Baal called on Baal from morning until noon but received no response.

questions.question: What did Elijah do at noon while the prophets of Baal were calling out?
questions.correctAnswer: He mocked them
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:27, Elijah mocked the prophets of Baal, sarcastically suggesting Baal might be busy, traveling, or sleeping and needed to be awakened.

questions.question: What did Elijah do to the altar of the LORD before the offering?
options: He built a new altar elsewhere
questions.correctAnswer: He repaired the broken altar
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:30 states that Elijah repaired the altar of the LORD that had been broken down before preparing for the offering.

questions.question: Why did Elijah take twelve stones according to 1 Kings 18:31?
options: To represent the twelve tribes of Israel
To build a wall around the altar
To mark the boundary of Mount Carmel
questions.correctAnswer: To represent the twelve tribes of Israel
questions.explanation: Elijah took twelve stones to symbolize the twelve tribes of the sons of Jacob, as Israel was the name given to them (1 Kings 18:31).

questions.question: What did Elijah instruct to pour on the burnt sacrifice and wood, and how many times was it done?
questions.correctAnswer: Water, three times
questions.explanation: Elijah commanded water to be poured on the sacrifice and wood three times, soaking everything and filling the trench around the altar (1 Kings 18:33-35).

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 18:24 teach about faith and trust in God through the contest setup in verse 23?
options: It shows that calling on God with faith will reveal His power
It emphasizes human effort over divine intervention
It promotes worship of multiple gods simultaneously
It suggests fire is a test of physical strength
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that calling on God with faith will reveal His power
questions.explanation: Verse 23 instructs preparing the sacrifice without fire, and verse 24 declares that the God who answers by fire is the true God, teaching faith in God's power to respond miraculously.

questions.question: What promise does 1 Kings 18:32 offer if the altar is rebuilt as instructed in verse 31?
options: God's presence will be demonstrated to Israel
The altar will never be broken again
The people will receive immediate rain
The prophets of Baal will be defeated by sword
questions.correctAnswer: God's presence will be demonstrated to Israel
questions.explanation: Rebuilding the altar with twelve stones representing the tribes (verse 31) sets the stage in verse 32 for invoking the LORD's name, showing His presence and authority among Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah told the people to come near after repairing the altar to witness God's power.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:30, after repairing the altar, Elijah called all the people to come near, preparing them to witness God's response by fire.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 18.

questions.question: What did Elijah do three times to the burnt sacrifice during the contest on Mount Carmel?
options: He called for fire from heaven
questions.correctAnswer: He poured water over it
questions.explanation: Elijah instructed that four barrels of water be poured over the burnt sacrifice and wood three times to make the altar drenched (1 Kings 18:33-34).

questions.question: How many stones did Elijah use to rebuild the altar of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve
questions.explanation: Elijah took twelve stones, representing the twelve tribes of Israel, and built the altar in the name of the LORD (1 Kings 18:31).

questions.question: What was the purpose of the trench Elijah made around the altar?
options: To contain two measures of seed
To separate the altar from the people
questions.correctAnswer: To contain two measures of seed
questions.explanation: Elijah made a trench about the altar as large as would contain two measures of seed, likely to hold water poured on the altar (1 Kings 18:32).

questions.question: Which phrase did Elijah use to address God in his prayer during the evening sacrifice?
options: LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel
God of the heavens and the earth
God of the prophets and kings
questions.correctAnswer: LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel
questions.explanation: Elijah prayed, calling on the LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel to show that He is God in Israel (1 Kings 18:36).

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people when fire from the LORD consumed the offering?
options: They fell on their faces and declared the LORD is God
questions.correctAnswer: They fell on their faces and declared the LORD is God
questions.explanation: The people fell on their faces and proclaimed, 'The LORD, he is the God; the LORD, he is the God' when the fire consumed the offering (1 Kings 18:39).

questions.question: After the contest, what did Elijah command to be done with the prophets of Baal?
options: They were taken and slain at the brook Kishon
They were allowed to leave quietly
questions.correctAnswer: They were taken and slain at the brook Kishon
questions.explanation: Elijah commanded to seize the prophets of Baal and they were killed at the brook Kishon (1 Kings 18:40).

questions.question: What sound did Elijah say he heard that indicated an abundance of rain was coming?
options: A sound of abundance of rain
questions.correctAnswer: A sound of abundance of rain
questions.explanation: Elijah told Ahab to eat and drink because he heard the sound of an abundance of rain (1 Kings 18:41).

questions.question: How many times did Elijah send his servant to look toward the sea before he saw a cloud?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven
questions.explanation: Elijah instructed his servant to go look toward the sea seven times before he saw a small cloud rising (1 Kings 18:43-44).

questions.question: What did the small cloud rising from the sea look like?
questions.correctAnswer: A man's hand
questions.explanation: The cloud appeared like a man's hand rising out of the sea, signaling the coming rain (1 Kings 18:44).

questions.question: What did Elijah do when the rain began to fall heavily?
options: He girded up his loins and ran ahead of Ahab
He sang a song of praise
questions.correctAnswer: He girded up his loins and ran ahead of Ahab
questions.explanation: Elijah, empowered by the LORD, ran ahead of Ahab to Jezreel after the rain started (1 Kings 18:46).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage is closely connected to Elijah's prayer invoking the LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 3:6
questions.explanation: Elijah's prayer references the covenant God revealed to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, echoing God's self-identification to Moses at the burning bush in Exodus 3:6.

questions.question: Which New Testament event echoes the theme of fire from heaven consuming a sacrifice as seen in Elijah's contest?
questions.correctAnswer: Pentecost with tongues of fire
questions.explanation: Pentecost in Acts 2 features tongues of fire, symbolizing God's powerful presence, reminiscent of the fire from heaven on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:38).

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'altar' (מִזְבֵּחַ, mizbeach) in this chapter?
options: A place of sacrifice and God's presence
questions.correctAnswer: A place of sacrifice and God's presence
questions.explanation: The altar (mizbeach) is the sacred place where sacrifices are offered and God's presence is manifested, central to Elijah's contest (1 Kings 18:30-32).

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Elijah's mocking of Baal's prophets, where he suggests Baal might be talking, pursuing, or sleeping?
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: Elijah uses irony to mock Baal's prophets by sarcastically suggesting their god could be busy or asleep, highlighting their impotence (1 Kings 18:27).

questions.question: True or False: Elijah prayed for rain only after the fire consumed the altar and the people acknowledged the LORD as God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Elijah first demonstrated God's power by fire; after the people confessed the LORD as God, Elijah prayed for rain, signaling the end of famine (1 Kings 18:38-41).

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by the fire of the LORD consuming the sacrifice, wood, stones, dust, and even licking up the water in 1 Kings 18:38?
options: God's omnipotence to perform miraculous acts
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence to perform miraculous acts
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:38 shows God's omnipotence as He miraculously consumes the offering and surrounding elements by fire, demonstrating His supreme power over nature. This is a direct divine intervention that only an omnipotent God could perform.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 18:19, what does Elijah's summoning of all Israel and the prophets of Baal symbolize about the nature of true worship?
options: The exclusivity of Yahweh as the only true God
The tolerance of many gods in Israel
The acceptance of syncretism in worship
The equality of Baal and Yahweh as gods
questions.correctAnswer: The exclusivity of Yahweh as the only true God
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:19, Elijah gathers Israel and Baal's prophets to contrast true worship of Yahweh with Baal worship, emphasizing that Yahweh alone is God. This underscores monotheism and rejects syncretism, affirming God's exclusive claim to worship.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's providence is illustrated by Elijah's prayer for rain after a long drought as described in 1 Kings 18:41-45?
options: God controls natural elements and sustains creation
Human effort alone can end a drought
Rain is a random natural occurrence
God is indifferent to human needs
questions.correctAnswer: God controls natural elements and sustains creation
questions.explanation: Verses 41-45 show Elijah praying and God sending abundant rain, illustrating God's providential control over weather and natural elements, sustaining life. This confirms the doctrine that God is sovereign over creation and responsive to His servants' prayers.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 18:12 reveal the tension between divine sovereignty and human fear in the life of Obadiah?
options: Obadiah fears God yet is afraid of man’s wrath
Obadiah trusts only in human power
Obadiah does not fear the LORD
Obadiah believes God will protect him without fear
questions.correctAnswer: Obadiah fears God yet is afraid of man’s wrath
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:12, Obadiah expresses fear of Ahab’s wrath despite his fear of the LORD, illustrating the tension between divine sovereignty and human threats. This depicts sanctification as a process amid trials where fear of God coexists with human fear.

questions.question: What theological significance does Elijah’s challenge to Israel in 1 Kings 18:21 carry about the nature of choice in salvation?
options: Humans must decisively choose whom to follow, God or idols
Salvation is automatic without human choice
God forces Israel to worship Him against their will
questions.correctAnswer: Humans must decisively choose whom to follow, God or idols
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:21 shows Elijah challenging Israel to choose between Yahweh and Baal, emphasizing human responsibility in faith decisions. This highlights the doctrine of free will in response to God's call, affirming the necessity of decisive faith.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the story of Elijah calling down fire is a myth. What does 1 Kings 18:36-38 actually teach about God's identity and power?
options: God is the one true God who powerfully answers by fire
God is silent and indifferent to human events
Baal is equally powerful as God
Fire was natural and unrelated to divine action
questions.correctAnswer: God is the one true God who powerfully answers by fire
questions.explanation: Verses 36-38 teach that God answered Elijah's prayer by sending fire, authenticating His identity as the one true God with power to intervene miraculously, which contradicts sceptical claims of myth. This affirms God's reality and authority.

questions.question: What doctrine about idolatry and false gods is taught by the failure of Baal’s prophets to elicit any response in 1 Kings 18:26-29?
options: False gods are powerless and silent
God allows multiple gods to answer prayers
questions.correctAnswer: False gods are powerless and silent
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:26-29 shows Baal’s prophets crying out without any response, teaching the doctrine that idols have no real power or voice, confirming that they are false gods and cannot save or answer prayer.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Elijah’s persistent prayer for rain as he sends his servant repeatedly to look toward the sea in 1 Kings 18:43-44?
options: God’s faithfulness and patience in answering prayer
God’s wrath and judgment without delay
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness and patience in answering prayer
questions.explanation: Elijah’s repeated sending of his servant (1 Kings 18:43-44) reflects God’s faithfulness to answer prayer in His timing, demonstrating His patience and sovereign control over events according to His perfect will.

questions.question: How does the division of the land between Ahab and Obadiah in 1 Kings 18:5-6 illustrate human cooperation under divine providence?
options: Humans use practical means while God directs ultimate outcomes
Humans alone control all events without divine involvement
God commands humans to avoid cooperation
questions.correctAnswer: Humans use practical means while God directs ultimate outcomes
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:5-6, Ahab and Obadiah divide the land to search for water, showing human responsibility and cooperation in action, while the broader narrative reveals God’s providential orchestration of events beyond human control.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do 1 Kings 18:3-4 and 1 Kings 18:40 provide about God's judgment and preservation of His faithful servants?
options: God preserves His faithful prophets while executing judgment on false prophets
God punishes all prophets equally without distinction
God ignores the plight of His faithful servants
God allows Baal’s prophets to remain unjudged
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves His faithful prophets while executing judgment on false prophets
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 describe Obadiah hiding and feeding 100 prophets to preserve them, while verse 40 narrates Elijah’s execution of Baal’s false prophets, showing God’s dual role of preservation for the faithful and judgment on the wicked.

questions.question: What does Elijah’s repairing of the altar with twelve stones in 1 Kings 18:30-31 symbolize about God's covenant and Israel's identity?
options: The unity of the twelve tribes under the covenant with God
The rejection of Israel’s tribal structure
The establishment of a new god
The division of Israel into two kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: The unity of the twelve tribes under the covenant with God
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:30-31, Elijah’s use of twelve stones represents the twelve tribes of Israel, symbolizing God's covenant people unified under His name, emphasizing continuity of God’s promises to Israel.

questions.question: How does Elijah’s statement in 1 Kings 18:18 about Ahab and his father's house illustrate the biblical theme of covenant unfaithfulness?
options: Ahab’s family forsook God’s commandments and followed Baalim
Ahab’s family were faithful to the covenant
The prophets of Baal were true followers of God
questions.correctAnswer: Ahab’s family forsook God’s commandments and followed Baalim
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:18 declares that Ahab and his lineage abandoned God's laws and followed Baal, highlighting covenant unfaithfulness, a key biblical theme where Israel’s leaders are judged for idolatry and disobedience.

questions.question: What synthesis about divine revelation and human response is demonstrated by Elijah’s confrontation in 1 Kings 18:22 and the people's silence in 1 Kings 18:21?
options: Despite clear revelation, humans often hesitate or refuse to respond
Humans always respond immediately to God’s revelation
God does not reveal Himself clearly to people
Silence means approval of Baal worship
questions.correctAnswer: Despite clear revelation, humans often hesitate or refuse to respond
questions.explanation: Verses 21 and 22 show Elijah boldly confronting Israel while the people remain silent, indicating that even with clear divine revelation, people may vacillate or refuse to commit, reflecting human spiritual weakness in responding to God.

questions.question: What does the account of Elijah running ahead of Ahab’s chariot in 1 Kings 18:46 signify about the empowerment of God’s servants?
options: God empowers His servants with strength beyond natural ability
Elijah was naturally faster than Ahab
God does not intervene in human strength
Elijah’s running is unrelated to divine power
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers His servants with strength beyond natural ability
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:46 states that the hand of the LORD was on Elijah, enabling him to run ahead of Ahab’s chariot, symbolizing divine empowerment and enabling of God’s servants for His purposes beyond normal human capacity.

questions.question: From 1 Kings 18:1-2, what does the timing of God's message to Elijah reveal about divine sovereignty in the midst of human suffering?
options: God acts in His perfect timing to bring restoration
God is indifferent to famine and suffering
Human suffering is random and without divine purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God acts in His perfect timing to bring restoration
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 describe God’s word coming to Elijah after many days of famine, indicating God’s sovereign timing in sending rain and relief, showing divine control over hardship and restoration.
